patch.title: Obama Targets Four Transnational Criminal Organizations With Sanctions
patch.description_medium: On July 25, 2011, President Barack Obama imposed financial sanctions on four transnational criminal organizations: the Brothers’ Circle, the Camorra, the Yakuza and Los Zetas. The order blocked their property under U.S. jurisdiction and prohibited transactions by U.S. persons. It also authorized sanctions against people or entities providing material support to designated organizations.
patch.description_long:
President Barack Obama signed Executive Order 13581 on July 25, 2011, creating a sanctions framework aimed at significant transnational criminal organizations. The order initially targeted the Brothers’ Circle, the Camorra, the Yakuza and Los Zetas. Treasury described the measure as a way to disrupt the groups’ economic power and protect financial markets.

The restrictions blocked property in the United States, or held by U.S. persons, in which the designated groups had an interest. U.S. persons were also prohibited from transacting with them. Treasury, consulting the Justice and State Departments, could designate additional individuals or entities that materially assisted or financed those already covered. The initial list spanned criminal networks associated with Eurasia, Italy, Japan and Mexico rather than one region. This financial measure accompanied the administration’s broader strategy against organized crime. It imposed restrictions on assets and transactions; the announcement did not itself report arrests, prosecutions or measured reductions in the groups’ activity.

patch.title: James Comey Succeeds Robert Mueller as FBI Director
patch.description_medium: James Comey was sworn in as the FBI’s seventh director on September 4, 2013, succeeding Robert Mueller. President Barack Obama nominated him in June, and the Senate confirmed the appointment. Comey brought experience as a federal prosecutor and deputy attorney general, followed by private-sector legal roles at Lockheed Martin and Bridgewater Associates.
patch.description_long:
James Comey took office as the seventh director of the Federal Bureau of Investigation on September 4, 2013, succeeding Robert Mueller. President Barack Obama had nominated him at a White House ceremony in June, and Senate confirmation preceded his swearing-in. The transition placed a former senior Justice Department official at the head of the bureau.

Comey had served as an assistant U.S. attorney in New York and Virginia before becoming the U.S. attorney for the Southern District of New York. He became deputy attorney general in 2003, then left government in 2005 for a legal leadership role at defense contractor Lockheed Martin. Five years later, he joined investment firm Bridgewater Associates as general counsel. His FBI tenure ran from September 2013 until May 2017, when President Donald Trump dismissed him. That later dismissal was a separate presidential action: the 2013 appointment originated with Obama and marked the beginning of Comey’s service, rather than a Trump appointment.
